This petition is filed by accused No.2 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the entire criminal proceedings in Spl.C.No.145/2022 registered by the Bagalagunte Police, Bengaluru, in Crime No.69/2020 and charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC, Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and Section 3(1)(r)(s) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Ordinance 2014 (hereinafter referred to as 'the SC and ST Act' for short).
2.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Ordinance 2014
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent No.1.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has remained absent.

3. The case of the prosecution is that respondent No.2 filed first information before Bagalagunte Police NC: 2024:KHC:45748 station on 07.03.2020 alleging that accused No.1, who is the son of the petitioner (accused No.2), had fallen in love with the complainant with an intent to marry her.

Accordingly, they married on 23.01.2019 at Kaveeramma Temple, situated at Electronic City,
Bengaluru.
Subsequent to the marriage, they stayed in the rented house and accused No.1 looked after the complainant very well for some time.
Thereafter, she becomes pregnant.
Accused No.1 gave intimation to the present petitioner (accused No.2), who is the mother of accused No.1.
The petitioner invited both son and daughter-in-law to their house.
Accordingly, the complainant and accused No.1 visited the house of the petitioner at Birur.
At that time, the petitioner informed accused No.1 that she wanted to perform Satyanarayana Pooja at home and thereby, she instructed her son to abort the fetus.
Subsequently, they returned to Bangalore and on the instruction of the petitioner, accused No.1 gave some tablets to the complainant and aborted the fetus.

After one Smt Renuka vs State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136535374/
2 month, they went to Birur for the ugadi festival.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At that time, the NC: 2024:KHC:45748 petitioner is said to have abused the complainant by stating that she belongs to a lower caste, she has not brought any dowry and she also informed that she could have got more dowry if her son married some other girl.
Subsequently, accused No.1 also started harassing the complainant, abusing her in filthy language by taking her caste and later, they shifted to Bengaluru and stayed in a rented house.
Accused No.1 abused her in filthy language and pressurised her to give consent for the divorce.
Accused No.1 also dropped the complainant to her sister's house on 09.02.2020 and thereafter, he did not return.
Hence, she lodged a complaint.

4. After lodging the FIR, the petitioner approached this Court by filing the criminal petition for quashing the criminal proceedings, which came to be dismissed and permitted the respondent to investigate the matter and accordingly, police investigated the matter.
Therefore, once again, the petitioner -accused No.2 is before this Court.

Learned counsel for the petitioner mainly contended that though the allegations against the petitioner are for the offences punishable under Section 3(1) (r)(s) of the SC and ST Act, the place where she is abused is said to be in the house at Birur, which is not a public place.
There is no other statement of the witnesses recorded by the investigating Officer.

Therefore, the offence committed within the house cannot be said to be offence punishable under Section 3(1)(r)(s) of the SC and ST Act and therefore, it is a fit case for quashing the proceedings and conducting a criminal trial would be an abuse of the process of law.

6. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State objected the petition, contending that accused Nos.1 and 2 jointly abused her taking her caste by using abusive words, which attracts Sections 504 and 506 of IPC.
Apart from the special Act, the case is required for trial.
Hence, she prays for dismissing the petition.
Having heard the arguments and perused the records, on perusal of the same, this court had already given findings during the crime stage in Crl.P.No.4956/2020 dated 20.09.2021.

On careful perusal of the statement of the complainant, where she has stated the marriage between the accused No.1 and the complainant was a love marriage, without the knowledge of the accused No.2 and the relative of the complainant, which is not in dispute.
Previously they have resided at Bagalkote and in another place in Bengaluru in a rented house.

Subsequently, the accused No.1 intimated this petitioner about the marriage and therefore the accused No.1 took the complainant to the house of accused No.2 at Birur, where the accused No.2, the present petitioner wanted to perform the 'Sathyanarayana Pooja' for that, she should not carry the child and she also was abused in filthy language, by taking the caste as she was from lower caste women and should not be allowed to perform the Pooja and the child was also not allowed to attend the Pooja.
However, taking the caste name and abused her in NC: 2024:KHC:45748 filthy language in the house of the accused No.2/present petitioner.

The further statement of the victim shows, the offence of abusing the Smt Renuka vs State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136535374/
3 complainant in filthy language, taking the caste name by this petitioner within the house was not seen by any other person.

entities.text: Smt Renuka vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The categorical statement of respondent No.2 reveals there was no other persons who have heard abusing the complainant/respondent No.2 by taking caste name which was within the house of accused No.2.

Subsequently, on 06.04.2019, the statement of the Narasimhamurthy who said to be brother-in-law of the complainant also says, the accused No.2 abused her in filthy language, taking the caste name in front of the house.
However, there is no statement of the neighbours were recorded at Birur to show that the offence attracts section 3(1)(r)(s) of SC/ST Act.

If the accused No.2 abused the complainant in filthy language by taking the caste name within the house, which is not in public view, therefore, the offence alleged against the accused No.2/the present petitioner will not attract under Section 3(1)(r)(s) of SC/ST Act.

However,
NC: 2024:KHC:45748 there are ingredients against the accused No.2 in respect of sections 504 and 506 of IPC for demand of dowry after their marriage, which also attracts section 4 of the DP Act.
She has insisted and harassed the complainant to abort the child and they should not attend the pooja and taking the caste name and insisted to abort the child and the abortion was also done.
There was harassment made by accused Nos.1 and 2 in respect of 498 (A) of IPC.
Therefore, against accused No.2, the sections 504 and 506 of IPC, 498A of IPC, apart from Section 4 of DP Act, attracts.
There are ingredients against accused No.1 also who is not before this court.
It is well settled under Section 220 of Cr.P.C., when the other accused were also there, there shall be a joint trial with both the accused.

Therefore, this petitioner also tried along with accused No.1 by the Special Court where the allegation made against accused No.1, which attracts section 3(1)(r)(s) of the SC and ST Act and other IPC offences.
Therefore, I proceed to pass the following order, NC: 2024:KHC:45748 ORDER
The petition is allowed in part.

The criminal proceedings against the petitioner in Spl.C.No.145/2022 registered in Crime No.69/2020 by the Bagalagunte Police, Bengaluru, pending on the file of II Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru Rural District, Bengaluru, for the offence under Section 3(1)(r)(s) of the SC and ST Act against this petitioner is hereby quashed.
